evidence_class: REST / live authenticated OpenSearch Security API enumeration (CURRENT)
method: All data below was obtained live via HTTP GET only against the OpenSearch Security API on two clusters. No PUT/POST/PATCH/DELETE was issued to any Security API endpoint. Cluster A (wazuh1.indexer:9200) was authenticated with the admin TLS client certificate registered in plugins.security.authcz.admin_dn; cluster B (shuffle-opensearch:9200) was authenticated with the existing internal admin identity whose credential was supplied to curl on stdin (never as an argv element, never echoed). Both calls used internal-CA validation (--cacert, ssl_verify_result=0) and hostname verification (--resolve to the certificate DNS SAN; no -k/--insecure).
secret_handling: Password hashes (the `hash` field of every internal user) and all credential values are OMITTED. They were never printed, logged, hashed, fingerprinted, compared, or persisted. Only non-secret identity names, role names, index patterns, allowed actions and mapping assignments are recorded.

candidate_causes_evaluated.why: The same request path returns ssl_verify_result=0 against the internal CA both before and after authentication; the 401 arrived over a fully validated TLS session.
The identical URL returns 200 with a full JSON body once an admin identity is presented; /_plugins/_security/api/{internalusers,roles,rolesmapping} all resolve.
The server answered with an HTTP 401 and body 'Unauthorized' - it was reachable and healthy.
No session or token was ever established; there is no session cause because no credential or client certificate was presented at all.

A permission failure by an authenticated principal returns 403 FORBIDDEN with an explanatory message (demonstrated live as negative test N6). Phase 84 received 401 with body 'Unauthorized', which is the pre-authentication class.

candidate_causes_evaluated.cause: Missing identity: no admin TLS client certificate and no credentials, with anonymous auth disabled
candidate_causes_evaluated.why: CONFIRMED. plugins.security.anonymous_auth_enabled=false (live securityconfig GET) and plugins.security.restapi.roles_enabled=[all_access, security_rest_api_access]. A request carrying no client certificate and no Authorization header therefore has no principal to evaluate and is rejected at the authentication stage with 401 before any authorization decision. Reproduced as N1; also reproduced with a valid-but-non-admin client certificate (N2, N3).

root_cause_analysis.conclusion: Identity/credential cause, not TLS, endpoint, permission, or session.
